passages.label: Title
passages.text:
COMMISSION REGULATION (EU) 2019/649
of 24 April 2019
amending Annex III to Regulation (EC) No 1925/2006 of the European Parliament and of the Council as regards trans fat, other than trans fat naturally occurring in fat of animal origin
(Text with EEA relevance)

passages.label: Document context
passages.text: THE EUROPEAN COMMISSION,

passages.label: Citation 1
passages.text: Having regard to the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union,

passages.label: Citation 2
passages.text: Having regard to Regulation (EC) No 1925/2006 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 20 December 2006 on the addition of vitamins and minerals and of certain other substances to foods ( 1 ) , and in particular Article 8(2) thereof,

passages.label: Document context
passages.text: Whereas:

passages.label: Recital 1
passages.text: (1) | In accordance with Regulation (EC) No 1925/2006, the Commission may, on its own initiative, take a decision to include a substance, other than a vitamin or mineral, or an ingredient containing such substance in Annex III to that Regulation, listing the substances whose use in foods is prohibited, restricted or under Union scrutiny, if that substance is associated with a potential risk to consumers as provided for in Article 8(1) of that Regulation.

passages.label: Recital 2
passages.text: (2) | On 4 December 2009, the European Food Safety Authority (hereinafter ‘the Authority’) adopted a scientific opinion ( 2 ) concluding that the intake of trans fatty acids should be as low as possible within the context of a nutritionally adequate diet.

passages.label: Recital 3
passages.text: (3) | On 3 December 2015, the Commission adopted a report on trans fats in foods and in the overall diet of the Union population ( 3 ) . The report recalled that coronary heart disease is the leading cause of death in the Union and a high intake of trans fats seriously increases the risk of heart disease, more than any other nutrient on a per calorie basis.

passages.label: Recital 4
passages.text: (4) | The report concluded that establishing a legal limit for industrial trans fats in food appears to be the most effective measure in terms of public health, consumer protection and compatibility with the internal market.

passages.label: Recital 5
passages.text: (5) | On 30 April 2018, the Commission asked the Authority to compile the outcomes of scientific advice already provided by the Authority on the health effects of trans fats, in particular on nutrition and health claims, dietary reference values and food additives; and to inform the Commission on how such scientific advice relates to current goals and recommendations on the intake of trans fats to maintain health.

passages.label: Recital 6
passages.text: (6) | On 19 June 2018, the Authority provided its conclusion in the form of scientific and technical assistance. It concluded ( 4 ) based on review of available scientific evidence that according to the latest national and international recommendations, dietary intakes of trans fatty acids should be as low as possible.

passages.label: Recital 7
passages.text: (7) | On 15 May 2018, the World Health Organisation called for the elimination of industrially-produced trans fatty acids from global food supply ( 5 ) .

passages.label: Recital 8
passages.text: (8) | Trans fat is a substance other than vitamins and minerals for which harmful effects on health have been identified. The substance should therefore be placed in Part B of Annex III to Regulation (EC) No 1925/2006 and its addition to foods or its use in the manufacture of foods should only be allowed under the conditions specified in that Annex, in view of the current state of scientific and technical knowledge.

passages.label: Recital 9
passages.text: (9) | The definitions of ‘fat’ and of ‘trans fat’ set out in Annex I of Regulation (EC) No 1169/2011 of the European Parliament and of the Council ( 6 ) and of ‘retail’ set out in Article 3(7) of Regulation (EC) No 178/2002 of the European Parliament and of the Council ( 7 ) should apply to the relevant terms in Part B of Annex III to Regulation (EC) No 1925/2006.

passages.label: Recital 10
passages.text: (10) | In order to facilitate the application of this Regulation, it is necessary to require from food business operators supplying food to other food business operators with the exception of retailers, to provide them with the information on the amount of trans fat, other than trans fat naturally occurring in fat of animal origin, where that amount exceeds 2 grams per 100 grams of fat.

passages.label: Recital 11
passages.text: (11) | In order to enable food business operators to adapt to the new requirements which will result from this Regulation, appropriate transitional measures should be adopted.

passages.label: Recital 12
passages.text: (12) | Regulation (EC) No 1925/2006 should therefore be amended accordingly.

passages.label: Recital 13
passages.text: (13) | The measures provided for in this Regulation are in accordance with the opinion of the Standing Committee on Plants, Animals, Food and Feed,

passages.label: Document context
passages.text: HAS ADOPTED THIS REGULATION:

passages.label: Article 1
passages.text:
Article 1
The content of trans fat, other than trans fat naturally occurring in fat of animal origin, in food intended for the final consumer and food intended for supply to retail, shall not exceed 2 grams per 100 grams of fat.

passages.label: Article 2
passages.text:
Article 2
Food business operators supplying other food business operators with food not intended for the final consumer or not intended for supply to retail, shall ensure that supplied food business operators are provided with information on the amount of trans fat, other than trans fat naturally occurring in fat of animal origin, where that amount exceeds 2 grams per 100 grams of fat.

passages.label: Article 3
passages.text:
Article 3
Part B of Annex III to Regulation (EC) No 1925/2006 is amended in accordance with the Annex to this Regulation.

passages.label: Article 4
passages.text:
Article 4
This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union .
Food which does not comply with this Regulation may continue to be placed on the market until 1 April 2021.

passages.label: Document context
passages.text:
This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.
Done at Brussels, 24 April 2019.
For the Commission
The President
Jean-Claude JUNCKER
( 1 ) OJ L 404, 30.12.2006, p. 26 .
( 2 ) EFSA Panel on Dietetic Products, Nutrition, and Allergies (NDA); Scientific Opinion on Dietary Reference Values for fats, including saturated fatty acids, polyunsaturated fatty acids, monounsaturated fatty acids, trans fatty acids, and cholesterol. EFSA Journal 2010; 8(3):1461.
( 3 ) COM(2015)619 final of 3.12.2015.
( 4 ) EFSA, 2018. Scientific and technical assistance on trans fatty acids. EFSA supporting publication 2018:EN-1433. 16 pp. doi:10.2903/sp.efsa.2018.EN-1433.
( 5 ) REPLACE – an Action package to eliminate industrially-produced trans fatty acids, reference WHO/NMH/NHD/18.4, May 2018.
( 6 ) Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 25 October 2011 on the provision of food information to consumers, amending Regulations (EC) No 1924/2006 and (EC) No 1925/2006 of the European Parliament and of the Council, and repealing Commission Directive 87/250/EEC, Council Directive 90/496/EEC, Commission Directive 1999/10/EC, Directive 2000/13/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council, Commission Directives 2002/67/EC and 2008/5/EC and Commission Regulation (EC) No 608/2004 ( OJ L 304, 22.11.2011, p. 18 ).
( 7 ) Regulation (EC) No 178/2002 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 28 January 2002 laying down the general principles and requirements of food law, establishing the European Food Safety Authority and laying down procedures in matters of food safety ( OJ L 31, 1.2.2002, p. 1 ).

passages.label: Annex 1
passages.text:
ANNEX
In Part B of Annex III to Regulation (EC) No 1925/2006 the following table is inserted:
‘PART B
Restricted substances
Restricted substance | Conditions of use | Additional requirements
Trans fat other than trans fat naturally occurring in fat of animal origin | Maximum 2 grams per 100 grams of fat in food intended for the final consumer and food intended for supply to retail | Food business operators supplying other food business operators with food not intended for the final consumer or not intended for supply to retail, shall ensure that supplied food business operators are provided with information on the amount of trans fat, other than trans fat naturally occurring in fat of animal origin, where that amount exceeds 2 grams per 100 grams of fat.’

impact_families.uncertainty: Article 2, recital 10 and the annex's substance description strongly support reading the omitted qualification into the clause.

impact_families.title: Possible narrower Spanish scope of trans-fat disclosure
impact_families.effect: After the transition, above-threshold food supplied for retail but not for final consumers could require disclosure under the English wording but fall outside the Spanish disclosure condition.
impact_families.rationale: Article 1 prohibits that concentration in retail-destined food under both versions. The conditional difference concerns additional information, without altering the common composition restriction.
impact_families.uncertainty: The retailer exclusion in recital 10 supports a common interpretation despite the different operative connectors.

impact_families.title: Possible narrower Bulgarian scope of trans-fat disclosure
impact_families.effect: After the transition, an above-threshold business-to-business supply intended for retail but not for final consumers could require disclosure under the English wording while falling outside the Bulgarian disclosure duty.
impact_families.rationale: Article 1 independently prohibits the excessive concentration in retail-destined food. The supported conditional consequence concerns additional disclosure, without changing the composition limit or marketing permission.
impact_families.uncertainty: Recital 10 supports harmonization; the incorporated retail definition is not reproduced.

impact_families.title: Possible narrower Czech scope of trans-fat disclosure
impact_families.effect: After the transition, above-threshold food supplied to another operator for retail but not for final consumers could attract the English disclosure duty while remaining outside the Czech duty.
impact_families.rationale: The composition prohibition already covers retail-destined food in both versions. The possible change concerns an accompanying information obligation rather than permission to supply excessive trans-fat concentrations.
impact_families.uncertainty: Recital 10 and the complementary composition restriction support harmonizing the destination conditions.

impact_families.title: Possible narrower Croatian scope of trans-fat disclosure
impact_families.effect: After the transition, above-threshold food supplied to another operator for retail but not for final consumers could attract the English disclosure duty while falling outside the Croatian duty.
impact_families.rationale: The annex preserves the concentration cap for each destination category. The conditional difference concerns accompanying information for food already prohibited by that cap, without changing marketing permission.
impact_families.uncertainty: Recital 10 supports harmonization. Article 4 does not establish that disclosure remained compulsory during the transition.

impact_families.title: Possible narrower Finnish scope of trans-fat disclosure
impact_families.effect: After the transition, an above-threshold business-to-business supply intended for retail but not for final consumers could require disclosure under the English wording but not the Finnish wording.
impact_families.rationale: Both versions independently restrict the concentration in food intended for either destination. The possible changed outcome is an additional disclosure obligation, without a changed composition limit or marketing permission.
impact_families.uncertainty: Recital 10 supports interpreting both disclosure provisions as complementary to the destination-based composition restriction.

legislation.title: REGULATION (EU) 2024/3228 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 19 December 2024 repealing Regulation (EU) No 524/2013, and amending Regulations (EU) 2017/2394 and (EU) 2018/1724 with regard to the discontinuation of the European Online Dispute Resolution Platform (Text with EEA relevance)

passages.label: Title
passages.text:
REGULATION (EU) 2024/3228 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL
of 19 December 2024
repealing Regulation (EU) No 524/2013, and amending Regulations (EU) 2017/2394 and (EU) 2018/1724 with regard to the discontinuation of the European Online Dispute Resolution Platform
(Text with EEA relevance)

passages.label: Document context
passages.text: THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND THE COUNCIL OF THE EUROPEAN UNION,

passages.label: Citation 1
passages.text: Having regard to the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, and in particular Article 114 thereof,

passages.label: Citation 2
passages.text: Having regard to the proposal from the European Commission,

passages.label: Citation 3
passages.text: After transmission of the draft legislative act to the national parliaments,

passages.label: Citation 4
passages.text: Having regard to the opinion of the European Economic and Social Committee ( 1 ) ,

passages.label: Citation 5
passages.text: Acting in accordance with the ordinary legislative procedure ( 2 ) ,

passages.label: Document context
passages.text: Whereas:

passages.label: Recital 1
passages.text: (1) | Regulation (EU) No 524/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council ( 3 ) established, and mandated the Commission to develop and maintain, the European Online Dispute Resolution Platform (the ‘ODR platform’) at Union level, offering a single point of entry to consumers and traders seeking the out-of-court resolution of disputes arising from online sales or service contracts.

passages.label: Recital 2
passages.text: (2) | The ODR platform takes the form of an interactive website where consumers are able to request traders to agree to use an alternative dispute resolution (ADR) entity that is listed on the ODR platform and that complies with Directive 2013/11/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council ( 4 ) .

passages.label: Recital 3
passages.text: (3) | Regulation (EU) No 524/2013 requires online traders and online marketplaces to provide, on their website, an easily accessible link to the ODR platform. That obligation, together with information campaigns organised by the Commission and national stakeholders, has brought between two and three million visitors to the ODR platform every year.

passages.label: Recital 4
passages.text: (4) | However, only a minority of visitors use the ODR platform to submit a complaint and only 2 % of those complaints receive a positive reply from traders, meaning that their request can be transmitted to an ADR entity listed on the ODR platform. All in all, this represents about 200 cases per year across the Union.

passages.label: Recital 5
passages.text: (5) | The Commission published a call for evidence on adapting out-of-court dispute resolution to digital markets, which ran from 28 September to 21 December 2022. The Commission concluded that the ODR platform had been used by only 5 % of consumers who responded to that call for evidence, and the majority of respondents considered that the ODR platform should be substantially improved or be discontinued as it was not cost-effective. The evidence strongly suggests that, given that no more than 200 cases are transferred per year to an ADR entity, further maintenance of the ODR platform does not correspond to the principles of efficiency and effectiveness as provided for in Regulation (EU, Euratom) 2024/2509 of the European Parliament and of the Council ( 5 ) .

passages.label: Recital 6
passages.text: (6) | The ODR platform should be discontinued and Regulation (EU) No 524/2013 should therefore be repealed. Appropriate time should be provided to ensure that ongoing cases can be adequately terminated.

passages.label: Recital 7
passages.text: (7) | Pursuant to Regulation (EU) No 524/2013, personal data related to a dispute is kept in the database established further to that Regulation for the time necessary to achieve the purposes for which the data were collected and to ensure that data subjects are able to access their personal data in order to exercise their rights. In accordance with Regulation (EU) No 524/2013, that data is to be automatically deleted at the latest six months after the date of conclusion of the dispute which has been transmitted to the ODR platform. The Commission should inform users of the ODR platform with ongoing cases of the discontinuation of the ODR platform in good time, and in any case at least four months before that platform is discontinued. The Commission should offer assistance to those users of the ODR platform who wish to retrieve data related to their cases.

passages.label: Recital 8
passages.text: (8) | As the ODR platform is referred to in other Union legal acts as a platform that enables consumers to request traders to agree to an out-of-court dispute resolution, those acts should be amended to remove references to the ODR platform. Regulations (EU) 2017/2394 ( 6 ) and (EU) 2018/1724 ( 7 ) of the European Parliament and of the Council should therefore be amended accordingly. Directives (EU) 2015/2302 ( 8 ) , (EU) 2019/2161 ( 9 ) and (EU) 2020/1828 ( 10 ) of the European Parliament and of the Council also contain references to Regulation (EU) No 524/2013. It is intended that those Directives be amended by a separate legal act,

passages.label: Document context
passages.text: HAVE ADOPTED THIS REGULATION:

passages.label: Article 1
passages.text:
Article 1
Regulation (EU) No 524/2013 is repealed with effect from 20 July 2025.

passages.label: Article 2
passages.text:
Article 2
1. The European Online Dispute Resolution Platform (the ‘ODR platform’) shall be discontinued.
2. The submission of complaints to the ODR platform shall be discontinued on 20 March 2025.
3. The Commission shall inform users of the ODR platform with ongoing cases of the discontinuation of the ODR platform by 20 March 2025 and offer such users assistance to retrieve data related to their cases and accessible to them, where they wish to do so.
4. At the latest by 20 July 2025, all information, including personal data, related to cases in the ODR platform shall be deleted.

passages.label: Article 3
passages.text:
Article 3
Amendment to Regulation (EU) 2017/2394
In the Annex to Regulation (EU) 2017/2394, point 22 is deleted.

passages.label: Article 4
passages.text:
Article 4
Amendment to Regulation (EU) 2018/1724
In Annex III to Regulation (EU) 2018/1724, point 7 is replaced by the following:
‘(7) | The list of alternative consumer dispute resolution entities established by the Commission pursuant to Article 20(4) of Directive 2013/11/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council ( *1 ) .

passages.label: Article 5
passages.text:
Article 5
Entry into force
This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union .

passages.label: Document context
passages.text:
This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.
Done at Brussels, 19 December 2024.
For the European Parliament
The President
R. METSOLA
For the Council
The President
BÓKA J.

( 2 ) Position of the European Parliament of 13 March 2024 (not yet published in the Official Journal) and position of the Council at first reading of 19 November 2024 (not yet published in the Official Journal). Position of the European Parliament of 17 December 2024 (not yet published in the Official Journal).
( 3 ) Regulation (EU) No 524/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 21 May 2013 on online dispute resolution for consumer disputes and amending Regulation (EC) No 2006/2004 and Directive 2009/22/EC (Regulation on consumer ODR) ( OJ L 165, 18.6.2013, p. 1 ).
( 4 ) Directive 2013/11/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 21 May 2013 on alternative dispute resolution for consumer disputes and amending Regulation (EC) No 2006/2004 and Directive 2009/22/EC (Directive on consumer ADR) ( OJ L 165, 18.6.2013, p. 63 ).
( 5 ) Regulation (EU, Euratom) 2024/2509 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 23 September 2024 on the financial rules applicable to the general budget of the Union ( OJ L, 2024/2509, 26.9.2024, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/2509/oj ).
( 6 ) Regulation (EU) 2017/2394 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 12 December 2017 on cooperation between national authorities responsible for the enforcement of consumer protection laws and repealing Regulation (EC) No 2006/2004 ( OJ L 345, 27.12.2017, p. 1 ).
( 7 ) Regulation (EU) 2018/1724 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 2 October 2018 establishing a single digital gateway to provide access to information, to procedures and to assistance and problem-solving services and amending Regulation (EU) No 1024/2012 ( OJ L 295, 21.11.2018, p. 1 ).
( 8 ) Directive (EU) 2015/2302 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 25 November 2015 on package travel and linked travel arrangements, amending Regulation (EC) No 2006/2004 and Directive 2011/83/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council and repealing Council Directive 90/314/EEC ( OJ L 326, 11.12.2015, p. 1 ).
( 9 ) Directive (EU) 2019/2161 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 27 November 2019 amending Council Directive 93/13/EEC and Directives 98/6/EC, 2005/29/EC and 2011/83/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council as regards the better enforcement and modernisation of Union consumer protection rules ( OJ L 328, 18.12.2019, p. 7 ).
( 10 ) Directive (EU) 2020/1828 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 25 November 2020 on representative actions for the protection of the collective interests of consumers and repealing Directive 2009/22/EC ( OJ L 409, 4.12.2020, p. 1 ).
